sections.content:
Population change in Darlington in 2032

The population in Darlington is projected to increase from 109,413 people in 2022 to 115,436 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 7,131 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Darlington
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Darlington, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 3,225, with 10,009 births and 13,234 deaths in Darlington between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Darlington by 2.9%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 7,131, with 57,023 people moving to the area and 49,892 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Darlington by 6.5%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is not projected to change the population substantially, with 1,731 people moving to the area and 1,741 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 2,069, with 4,709 people moving to the area and 2,640 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Darlington by 1.9%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Darlington in 2032

The median age in Darlington is projected to rise from 43 years in 2022 to 44 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 23% of the population in Darlington are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 20% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Darlington between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Darlington is projected to stay the same, at around 62%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 314 to 345 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Darlington?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 22% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Darlington between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
